mappings.note: Gloss of the Braj word 'taruvar'. LO-70 covers curiosity about new words and their meanings; rejected LO-67, since no point of the dohe's content is being located.
Gloss of 'bipati'. LO-70 word meaning.
Gloss of 'chhitkaay'. LO-70 word meaning.
Gloss of 'sujan'. LO-70 word meaning.
Gloss of 'sarvar'. LO-70 word meaning.
Gloss of 'saanche'. LO-70 word meaning.
Gloss of 'kapal'. LO-70 word meaning; these seven form a Braj-vocabulary set for the dohe.

Asks the bhav of the 'jihva bavari' doha - attending to and appreciating the couplet's figurative language, which is LO-75's business (lay-tuk, chhand, muhavare, lokokti). Rejected LO-67, which is for locating a stated point.
Asks the bhav of the needle-and-sword doha; the point lies in the figure, not on the surface. LO-75 over LO-67.
Places Rahim in the Bhaktikaal - a question about the kinds and periods of Hindi composition, LO-69. Rejected LO-67, which concerns a point inside the text.
The poet's century, from the kavi-parichay - a specific point in the printed material, LO-67.
The language of his verse (Braj) is stated in the author note. LO-67. Rejected LO-72, which is about conversing on linguistic and cultural diversity, not recalling a stated fact.
'laghu ka arth' is a pure word-meaning item. LO-70.
Which word the doha applies to the tongue - locating the word in the couplet, LO-67. Rejected LO-75, since the pupil only has to find it, not interpret the figure.
Matches three dohe to their bhavarth - reading each couplet's figurative sense, LO-75. Rejected LO-70, because whole couplets rather than words are being glossed.
'explain_lines' on the doha about brief adversity - appreciating and unpacking the couplet's language, LO-75.
'explain_lines' on the tongue-and-skull doha - the sense lies wholly in the figure, so LO-75.
Asks in what sense the needle and sword are used - reading the doha's images, LO-75 rather than LO-67.
'prakriti hamein kya seekh deti hai' asks for the doha's overall lesson - LO-66, forming a sense of the composition's point, rather than LO-67's specific detail.
Why the thread of love must not be snapped turns entirely on the doha's metaphor of the knot. LO-75.
The whole item rests on the pun in 'pani' (water / lustre / honour) - appreciating the couplet's play of language, LO-75. Rejected LO-70, since one dictionary meaning will not do.
Why one should speak thoughtfully is the doha's stated counsel - locating and concluding, LO-67.
Asks the pupil to argue that the dohe are still relevant - an opinion on what has been read, LO-68. Rejected LO-67, which stops at the text.
The reason for not discarding the small is given in the couplet itself - locating and concluding, LO-67.

'talvar shabd kiska prateek hai' is a symbol question, so LO-75. NB the printed key is circular and useless - it says the word 'talvar' is a symbol of talvar, where the doha makes it the symbol of the great or large.
Why the good accumulate wealth is stated in the couplet. LO-67.
Which thread is meant - locating it in the doha. LO-67; rejected LO-75, as no interpretation is asked for.
Turns on the double sense of 'choon' (lime and flour) inside the pani doha - LO-75's appreciation of the couplet's wordplay.
Asks what 'pani' stands for in the case of a person (honour) - reading the doha's figure, LO-75.
Why brief adversity is called good is stated in the second line of the couplet. LO-67.
Why the tongue is called 'bavari' rests on the comparison with a madman - LO-75.
The 'skull being beaten' is figurative and must be read as such - LO-75 rather than LO-67.
How people behave when one is prosperous is stated in the couplet - locating and concluding, LO-67.
The mark of a true friend is stated in the doha. LO-67.

Padyansh with five sub-questions: some are comprehension of the couplet (LO-67), three ask what the sword and needle SYMBOLISE and what the line's aashay is (LO-75). Both cited so neither half is left unmapped.
Padyansh on the taruvar doha: four comprehension sub-questions (LO-67) plus an explicit word-meaning question on 'parkaaj' (LO-70).
Padyansh on the thread-of-love doha where every sub-question asks for an aashay - reading the couplet's figure throughout, LO-75.
Padyansh on the pani doha, whose sub-questions work the pun across moti, manush and choon - LO-75's appreciation of wordplay.
Padyansh on the bipada doha: comprehension sub-questions (LO-67) plus a word-meaning question on 'jagat' (LO-70).

Padyansh on the jihva doha: Q1 glosses 'jihva' (LO-70) while the rest read the figure of the mad tongue and the beaten skull (LO-75). NB the stem drops the initial letter of 'Rahiman', printing 'himan'.
Padyansh on the sampati-sage doha - five comprehension sub-questions on what the couplet states about wealth and true friends, LO-67.
Two demands: why the poet chose the thread image (LO-75, appreciating the couplet's figure) and what image the pupil would substitute, with reasons (LO-77, expressing one's own comment in writing).
Asks which human quality the nature imagery conveys (LO-75) and what else nature teaches, in the pupil's own words (LO-77).
